text:
[RFCS.10.1] A `ClockAdvance` atom records a new sample of the engine's two
clocks ([LTIM.2.8.5]): `clock_ns` is the monotonic clock ([LTIM.2.8.2]) and
`wall_ns` the wall clock ([LTIM.2.8.3]). Every `ClockAdvance` carries both,
whichever of them moved. `has_wall` is false when the wall clock has no value,
and `wall_ns` then carries nothing; the engine **must** write `has_wall` on
every `ClockAdvance`.  Clock advances are input events ([LFST.6.1]) and are
required for replay: without them, time-bound rules
(`after:`, TTL expirations, `cooldown:` windows) fire at different
times during replay, breaking determinism.

idris.name: Rfcs_10_1__atom
idris.note: What the recorder writes: a `ClockAdvance` carrying one sample -- both clocks together, whichever moved -- or the record of a step's input.
